title: Ratio Analysis
description: Interpret financial ratios and write a short credit memo. Tests financial analysis and the ability to explain numbers in plain English.

seo.overviewTitle: Financial Ratio Analysis & Business Performance Benchmarking
seo.overviewBody: Financial ratios evaluate a company's financial health, operational efficiency, and profitability trends. Financial analysts use liquidity ratios (Current/Quick), solvency metrics (Debt-to-Equity, Interest Coverage), efficiency numbers (Inventory Turnover), and DuPont ROE breakdowns to assess credit risk.

deliverables.title: 1. Financial Ratio Diagnostic & Benchmarking Spreadsheet
deliverables.desc: Comprehensive spreadsheet workbook computing multi-year liquidity, solvency, activity, and profitability ratios.

deliverables.title: 2. Executive Financial Health Analysis Memo
deliverables.desc: Analytical memo evaluating financial strengths, balance sheet vulnerabilities, and industry peer benchmark comparisons.

deliverables.title: 3. DuPont 3-Step ROE Decomposition Model
deliverables.desc: DuPont model breaking Return on Equity into Net Profit Margin, Asset Turnover, and Financial Leverage components.

faqs.question: What does a DuPont 3-Step ROE breakdown reveal?
faqs.answer: DuPont analysis breaks ROE into Profitability (Net Margin), Operational Efficiency (Asset Turnover), and Financial Leverage (Equity Multiplier) to pinpoint exact return drivers.

faqs.question: What is a healthy Current Ratio benchmark?
faqs.answer: A Current Ratio between 1.5 and 2.0 is generally considered healthy, indicating sufficient short-term assets to cover immediate liabilities without excess idle capital.

faqs.question: Why is the Quick Ratio (Acid-Test) more conservative than the Current Ratio?
faqs.answer: The Quick Ratio excludes inventory from current assets because inventory cannot be converted into cash immediately during liquidity crises.
